newsitem.title: USA: Tennessee lowers estimate of USG gas cuts.
newsitem.headline: Tennessee lowers estimate of USG gas cuts.

text.p: Tennessee Gas Pipeline Co, a unit of El Paso Energy, said Friday it lowered its estimate of U.S. Gulf natural gas output cuts on its system to 500 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) due to Hurricane Danny.

"In the last 15 minutes, it appears conditions on Tennessee Gas Pipeline are beginning to improve. Tennessee is now experiencing approximately 500 mmcfd loss of supply on its 500 and 800 supply lines," the company said in a notice to customers posted at 1630 EDT.

Tennessee is requiring customers to adjust nominations to reflect production losses and balance for these losses by securing alternate supplies or utilizing storage. As conditions begin to improve, Tennessee will allow shippers to bring their markets back, the notice said.
Earlier today, the company said about 600 mmcfd had been cut on its system by producers.
Danny was upgraded to a hurricane last night when sustained winds exceeded 74 mph.

At 1400 EDT, the storm was located at latitude 29.6 north, longitude 89.1 west, or about 60 miles east-southeast of New Orleans, moving northeast at about five mph with maximum sustained winds of 75 mph.
Danny was on track to make landfall in the next 24 hours somewhere on the Mississippi/Alabama coast.
